approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a molecular graph tree from accepted molecules, purchases a fresh frontier directly, and backs each real return up only its generating occurrence path. Selection shares receipt-backed maximum returns between chemically similar sibling graphs and accounts for pending purchases. It begins with the supplied root forest; after an observed strict improvement, it clears the tree and starts a fresh episode at the new incumbent, using that molecule’s original receipt as one cached root context while retaining the global accepted archive.
approach.novelty: Retain the incumbent from immediately before the feedback boundary as a second fresh origin alongside the new incumbent. Both origins compete under the existing peak-based selector, so a recently productive alternative can receive further graph edits after promotion. This changes fresh-root membership only. The earlier root-mean experiment spread purchases among the original roots and lost useful conversion; this extension retains peak selection and chooses its second origin from actual recent incumbent history. The assigned sibling experiments change exhausted-support routing, donor access or deeper return sharing instead.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-e4b751133c75 preserves only the newest accepted incumbent as the next episode origin, removing the preceding incumbent’s direct root access along with all previous topology. Its complete Search mean is 0.49949631467224465 (population SD 0.014066662744436314), a +0.15139519654635733 paired gain over n-85acb9fe7124 with positive changes on all three seed macros. Its lifecycle is functional: all 114 eligible promotions obtain accepted descendants, but 2779 occurrence occupancies are discarded. The utility of abandoned alternatives is unknown, so the bottleneck is missing alternative-origin access, not an established lost reward. Full/late incumbent increment masses are 4.365063054449033 and 1.3674630683963998 on 4350/2175 paid receipts; every zaleplon session has zero late gain. n-ae947f0cf21c supplies direct contrary evidence to breadth-as-utility: its root-mean/direct-frontier combination broadened original-root coverage but lost 0.06587415658432433 and reduced full/late conversion. This Child retains the functioning lifecycle and peak consumer while testing one recent observed alternative. The formal Anchor mean 0.607030316211131 remains a separate target; lower-Parent progress does not achieve it. Sources read: nodes/n-e4b751133c75/analysis.json, nodes/n-85acb9fe7124/analysis.json, nodes/n-ae947f0cf21c/analysis.json, all Parent per-Search-seed summary.json and run.log files named by focus.artifacts.parent_evaluations, and the Parent implementation. Independent per-cell source/receipt checks and file hashes are recorded in policy/scratch/r0055-00-improve-L01/plan_evidence_manifest.json and its audit-seed-<Search seed>-<task>.json files, each citing its exact underlying log and trajectory. These reproduce 114 promotions, 114 accessed origins and 2779 discarded occupancies without oracle access.

hypothesis: Modify only the membership of each already-eligible fresh-root episode. At the beginning of observe capture the earliest accepted global incumbent record before any feedback from that boundary. After every pending return has been reconciled, when the inherited strict-improvement-and-positive-remaining-budget trigger fires, initialize exactly two fresh roots in order [new earliest accepted global incumbent, captured pre-observe incumbent]. Each distinct root receives exactly its own original accepted receipt as one cached context return. All old topology and visits are discarded as in the Parent; the initial supplied forest and trigger remain unchanged. The two origins compete through the inherited count-Tanimoto sibling peak B/D plus pending exploration. This is a single origin-membership intervention whose necessary consequences include two-root competition and a super-root normalized by two real cached contexts plus new episode purchases; it does not separately identify breadth, context or competition mediation.

finding_summary.headline: Both fresh origins received descendants, but late useful conversion fell 37% and mean score fell 0.01853.
finding_summary.insights:
Keeping a recent alternative can preserve useful proposals without blocking access to the newest incumbent, but access alone does not preserve refinement quality. Almost 47% of post-promotion purchases went to the preceding origin. Its 47 improvements did not offset the lost gain mass elsewhere, even though the total number of strict improvements stayed at 148. The late result was also more concentrated: one receipt supplied 43% of late gain and one session supplied 51%. This settles the registered two-origin adjustment under this complete panel, not the wider tree approach or the Parent’s established restart capability; whether breadth, competition or changed proposal paths caused the loss remains unresolved. The borrowed solution-to-origin element operated, while the simultaneous two-root adaptation failed its own benefit prediction, so the result is not a verdict on the source algorithm.

The trajectories show a limitation of the search method beyond root access. Typed scaffold coverage rose from 1,704 to 1,837, yet fragment-excluded within-session molecular similarity also rose, especially late, from 0.42764 to 0.46865. Broad aggregate coverage therefore coexists with increasingly local refinement. Internal failed routes fell from 541 to 146, but that efficiency improvement did not translate into higher scores. Molecular assessment finds useful ring/amine/carbonyl arrangements mixed with 319 tiny fragments, 244 molecules above fifty heavy atoms, reactive heteroatom linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Useful structures are reachable; their relationships are not reliably preserved during graph edits. A proposal operator that makes coherent scaffold or fragment changes while preserving those relationships is a plausible way to address this limitation, but this experiment does not establish its benefit or select its recipe. Neither additional root access nor fewer invalid actions alone resolves that structural limitation.
finding_summary.results: The extra origin was fully active: all 115 preceding-incumbent roots produced accepted descendants, totaling 1,686 purchases, while all 115 current-incumbent roots also remained accessible and supplied 1,894 purchases. The Parent supplied 3,580 purchases from its single current origin. The preceding origins produced 47 strict incumbent improvements, so their access was real and sometimes useful. They nevertheless failed to improve total conversion: late gain per paid molecule fell from 0.00062872 to 0.00039798, and full gain per paid molecule fell from 0.00100346 to 0.00093958. Current-origin first access remained immediate, but only 72 of 115 current origins produced a global improvement, compared with 101 of 114 Parent origins. All fifteen sessions completed and receipt, root-membership and selection checks found no mismatch. The complete paired mean score fell from 0.499496 to 0.480970, a change of −0.018526; eight task/seed endpoints improved, six declined and one tied. Two of three seed means declined. The frozen +0.002 Parent utility criterion failed, and the result remained 0.126060 below the formal Anchor. The registered late-conversion and endpoint predictions are refuted; execution and descendant access are supported.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and amino chemistry coexists with fragments, reactive linkages and stereochemically unspecified polycycles.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment concerns n-b13ef5ae4ba8 and published code Parent n-e4b751133c75, using only the complete frozen Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2. context.comparison independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all Child and Parent trajectory paths exist, with no missing task or absent pairing. Each side contains 4500 accepted rows, including 4350 optimizer proposals; initial observations are excluded from proposal descriptors. The chemistry is broad: indole carboxamides, fused nitrogen/sulfur heteroaromatics, ring-bound tertiary amines, carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, partly saturated fused rings and crowded amino/oxygen cages. The Child median is 26 heavy atoms, with a range of 1 to 117. It has 3918 ring-bearing and 3365 aromatic-ring-bearing proposals; Parent has 3762 and 3396. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold identities total 1837/1284 for Child and 1704/1240 for Parent across the pooled accepted proposal sets. These are graph-identity counts, not evidence of useful diversity. The Child has 319 proposals below six heavy atoms and 244 above fifty, compared with Parent 425 and 301; the aggregate reduction does not hold for every task. Digest ring-closure-token rates span 0.8609 to 0.9379, supporting rich rings; aromatic-token rates span 0.4839 to 0.8805, so the output is not uniformly aromatic. Those digest counters measure SMILES presence, not atom fractions or RDKit ring perception. Conventional amide, ether and amine motifs make portions of the output recognizable medicinal chemistry. N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-O/N-N/thiocarbonyl combinations, heavily connected cages and very large recombinants make synthetic plausibility questionable overall; no synthesis, stability, exposure or biological-activity claim follows from the scores. All Child proposal strings lack tetrahedral stereo tokens and explicit charges; the former coexists with 2566 rows containing potential stereocentres under RDKit perception. Neutral SMILES do not imply absence of potentially basic amines. Last trajectory rows are merely final proposals and can score far below the best observed molecule. Per-task comparisons below concern observed chemistry and stored scores, not mechanism activation, component contribution or campaign selection. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0055-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence_manifest.json (SHA256 53013e25f266443110e21636a450a075c6d359de225c2ea1f25f3a05d1d9b3d2), which lists every existing underlying input, per-task audit, source hash and original staging path. Child snapshots preserve the exact trusted bytes under policy/scratch/r0055-00-improve-L01/molecular/inputs; no future node archive is cited as existing. RDKit descriptors and provenance are recorded in policy/scratch/r0055-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and the manifest's individual audit files.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 24 heavy atoms, range 1 to 62, with 57 below six and 26 above fifty. Digest ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9253/0.8805. The best observed proposal is a 25-heavy-atom indole carboxamide with three aromatic rings overall: an indole, a fluorophenyl substituent on a tertiary N-methyl amide, and an aminomethyl ether substituent. Other leaders are fused lactam-like polyaromatics or indole/furan/anilino heteroaromatics. This is substantial ring chemistry, with recognizable amide and ether building blocks, alongside more difficult fused analogues and fragments. Parent proposals have the same median size, but 101 below-six and 15 above-fifty rows. Parent leaders likewise contain fused aromatic/polar frameworks; this is not acquisition of rings from an acyclic baseline.
liabilities: The aminomethyl ether is an N,O-containing acetal-like linkage deserving stability scrutiny; other proposals introduce N-S or O-halogen linkages and highly fused frameworks.
Tiny heteroatom fragments and excessive polyaromatic concatenation both remain present; synthetic feasibility is not established by graph validity.
missing_features: Low-scoring fragments lack the connected aromatic surface plus localized carboxamide/amine/ether arrangement present in the leaders. This arrangement is reachable but not consistently retained during size and topology changes.

Close, chemically conventional alternatives across distinct ring arrangements are unevenly represented among the leaders; the trajectories do not identify a specific unseen target scaffold or required functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole secondary carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The aminomethyl-ether/N-methyl carboxamide leader scores 0.42762099872850584; removal of one aryl fluorine in a close analogue gives 0.42124582919382697, and replacing the aminomethyl ether substituent with an aminomethyl substituent gives 0.4175635604843711. These local observations associate the retained indole/carboxamide/aromatic arrangement and peripheral substitutions with higher scores, without identifying an independent causal contribution for each group. NF scores 0.0. A much larger 62-heavy-atom polyaromatic recombination scores 9.057737070109592e-50, so merely accumulating rings is not rewarded here. The Child best is slightly above the Parent best 0.42348216717712805 in seed 0, while its other seed maxima remain below their Parent counterparts.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 31 heavy atoms, range 1 to 117, with 60 below six and 87 above fifty. Digest ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9184/0.8667. The best proposal is a 26-heavy-atom structure with three aromatic rings: a fused sulfur/nitrogen bicyclic heteroaromatic core, methoxy groups and a difluoropyridylamino group linked through an N,O-substituted methine. Other high rows retain this core while adding another heteroaryl ether or changing peripheral substituents. Other seeds explore heavily fused nitrogen heteroaromatics and coumarin-like carbonyl rings. Parent has 74 below-six and 133 above-fifty rows. Both sides can generate extensive aromatic frameworks; the Child remains locally concentrated around related heteroaromatic families despite broad total scaffold variety.
liabilities: Several near-leading molecules contain O-F or O-O bonds; the leading N,O-substituted methine has unspecified stereochemistry and potential linkage stability concerns.
The largest molecules concatenate many ring systems and polar linkages, creating substantial synthesis and conformational burdens while retaining a moderate score.
missing_features: Floor-scoring small molecules lack the linked heteroaromatic surfaces and distributed donor/acceptor substituents of the leaders. Those features are not missing globally, but their relationships are not preserved in many smaller proposals.

A consistently stable, synthetically straightforward set of alternatives to the high-scoring N,O-acetal-like and reactive heteroatom variants is not demonstrated. The trajectories do not reveal a particular missing reference scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed range is 0.5 to 0.5966919537370974. Simple CCO and CNc1ccccc1 lie at the 0.5 floor, whereas the fused sulfur/nitrogen heteroaromatic aminoether scores 0.5966919537370974. A closely related analogue with an O-F bond scores 0.5965270426936842, as does a peroxide-bearing analogue, showing that this score does not cleanly distinguish those chemical liabilities. A 117-heavy-atom recombinant still scores 0.5714074839471548, so the observed gradient favors particular aromatic/polar connectivity over bare fragments but does not establish a universal size penalty. The published Parent seed-1 leader scores 0.6354531001589825 and is an N-rich heteroaryl ether with an N-Br bond; its higher score supplies no evidence of improved synthetic quality. Child maxima are above Parent in seeds 0 and 2 and below it in seed 1.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 29 heavy atoms, range 1 to 79, with 36 below six and 57 above fifty. Digest ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9379/0.8632. The best proposal has 28 heavy atoms and three rings, two aromatic: fluoroanisole and pyridine joined through alkyl/alkenyl substituents to a fluorinated azetidine carrying a tertiary amine. Close leaders include a pyrrolidine analogue and more rigid fused versions. Another high family carries N-methylpyrrolidine groups on a larger aromatic framework. These are accessible classes of medicinal-chemistry motifs in principle, though the exact substituted molecules have no demonstrated synthesis. Parent also reaches aromatic amino frameworks; its below-six/above-fifty counts are 102/54, so the Child reduction in tiny fragments does not remove its large-molecule tail.
liabilities: Some high molecules place fluorine on a congested small-ring carbon, carry several potentially stereogenic elements, or combine flexible hydrocarbon linkers with multiple aromatic groups; their conformational and stereochemical behavior remains unresolved.
Other high rows add O-S linkages or an acyl fluoride. High scores do not establish stability, selectivity, solubility or synthetic practicality.
missing_features: Many low rows lack the connected aromatic/amine architecture of the leaders; even low rows that contain an amine do not supply the same surrounding geometry and substitution pattern. This is inconsistent assembly of features, not absence of basic nitrogen from the generator.
Substituted saturated rings and alkenes are not represented with explicit stereochemical alternatives. Their effect on this score is not measured by the supplied trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyridyl/tertiary-amine leader scores 0.9955091591007366, the corresponding pyrrolidine analogue 0.9953653715789865, and the close phenyl analogue 0.9818923071433182. In contrast, a fluorobiphenyl acetanilide scores 0.00010717283327755194. A ring tertiary amine bearing hydroxamate and carboxanilide groups also scores only 0.0001331564383507784, so amine presence alone is insufficient. The visible association is with the arrangement of ring-associated potentially basic centres, aromatic surfaces and connecting geometry. A small fluoroanisole scores 0.0005066906630195705. Child seed-0 best 0.7348361230868937 remains below Parent 0.9190747819767275, while the other Child seed maxima are higher; no single chemistry association explains that mixed comparison or establishes physical binding.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 31 heavy atoms, range 1 to 107, with 89 below six and 66 above fifty. Digest ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.8609/0.7828. The best proposal has 33 heavy atoms and four rings, three aromatic: a nitrogen-rich fused dione ring system bearing an aminophenyl group and an ethoxy/acetyl-substituted phenyl group. Close leaders replace acetyl by methyl ester or adjust amine and peripheral ring atoms. This family supplies ordinary carbonyls, ethers and amino functionality in a complex but chemically legible scaffold. Other seeds reach sulfonamide-containing fused frameworks or heterocycles with an O-F group. Parent shows 71 below-six and 74 above-fifty rows, so the Child here produces more tiny fragments despite the panel-wide reduction.
liabilities: Some high alternatives introduce O-F bonds or highly fused nitrogen-rich ring systems. The best family is more conventional in its bond types, but feasibility of constructing its exact fused core is untested.
Small heteroatom fragments and oversized composites remain common enough to coexist with the chemically coherent leaders.
missing_features: Many proposals lack the leaders' coupled aromatic substitution and ring-integrated carbonyl arrangement, although both are clearly reachable. Ring opening or excessive concatenation does not reliably preserve that arrangement.

The modest observed ceiling does not identify an unseen required scaffold. It supports a gap in productive, chemically coherent alternatives around the observed motifs rather than a claim that ring or carbonyl chemistry is absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The acetyl/ethoxy/aminophenyl fused dione scores 0.2096115099737028; its methyl-ester analogue scores 0.20519851252137408, and methylating the aniline nitrogen of that analogue gives 0.20096750175337744. These are local associations around a retained aromatic/dicarbonyl arrangement. N=CN, C=N and S score 0.0; a 107-heavy-atom concatenation scores 0.08705443892371527. The score does not simply increase with molecular size or heteroatom count. The Parent seed-2 best scores 0.19720265943665388 and contains O-Cl; the higher Child best has conventional carbonyl/ether/amine functionality instead. This is evidence that a reactive O-halogen bond is not necessary for reaching this observed score range. In seed 0, the best paid proposal is 0.16099606343470504, below the initial best 0.1678386594791329; that shared initial molecule remains the endpoint incumbent on both sides.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 21 heavy atoms, range 1 to 57, with 77 below six and 8 above fifty. Digest ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.8609/0.4839: this population has abundant rings but substantially less aromatic content than the other populations. The best proposal is a compact 22-heavy-atom, five-ring cage with two aromatic rings, a pyrrolic nitrogen, oxygen bridges, amino groups and an N-fluoro-N-methyl substituent. Another high family combines a hydroxylated hydrazine/thiocarbonyl chain with partially saturated fused rings. Seed 2 reaches halogenated amino/acetal-like cages with O-F and N-O linkages. Parent has 77 below-six and 25 above-fifty rows; its aromatic-ring-bearing count is 588 versus Child 421. The Child therefore shifts toward nonaromatic compact polycycles, without making those exact crowded structures straightforward synthetic targets.
liabilities: N-fluoro amines, O-F bonds and hydroxylated hydrazine/thiocarbonyl linkages raise chemical stability and handling questions not resolved by the observed score.
Crowded bridged polycycles and unspecified stereochemistry make exact synthesis and molecular identity difficult to assess; extreme assemblies amplify those concerns.
missing_features: The observed high-scoring compact polar patterns are not consistently retained under expansion, fusion and heteroatom edits. Merely adding amines, oxygen atoms or rings does not reproduce the leaders' arrangement.

Chemically conservative alternatives to the high-scoring N-F, N-O and hydrazine/thiocarbonyl motifs are not consistently demonstrated in comparable local neighborhoods. The data do not establish that any one named reference motif is missing.
The cage-rich output lacks explicit stereochemical specification despite multiple potential stereocentres; no preferred configuration can be inferred from these records.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cage bearing methylamino substitution scores 0.4076078874136615, versus 0.34661951620817005 for its closely related methoxy analogue. A separate hydroxylhydrazine/thiocarbonyl fused-ring molecule scores 0.35235865253927606. These examples associate particular compact polar arrangements with higher scores, but their distinct scaffolds do not reveal one required motif. A 57-heavy-atom concatenation of related complex units scores 3.3612621572558883e-77, and a very large oxygen-rich cage assembly scores 0.0; retaining fragments of a productive structure while multiplying size is not sufficient. The Child seed-2 best is only 0.19754750998843454 despite a densely functionalized ring system; Parent there reaches 0.36108629330282105 with a different amino/acetal/heteroaryl arrangement. Child seed 1 is above its Parent, while seeds 0 and 2 are below; increased compactness or decreased aromaticity cannot be assigned a universal benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-b13ef5ae4ba8, complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, compared descriptively with published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 under the same profile. Leaders include indole carboxamides, aromatic ring-associated tertiary amines and fused diones, yet the Child still emits 319 below-six-heavy-atom fragments and 244 above-fifty-heavy-atom assemblies among 4350 proposals, versus Parent 425 and 301. Some large assemblies retain moderate scores while others approach zero. Thus this is inconsistent preservation of structural relationships, not evidence of a universal optimal size or missing ring-generation ability. Chemistry association is not component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful ring and polar-group relationships while changing molecular size and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Supply task-agnostic contraction, expansion and scaffold rearrangement alternatives that can retain informative local donor/acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships. Let current-session accepted observations determine which combinations and sizes are useful. These observations justify neither a fixed size floor nor a required named scaffold, and do not establish that any particular operator caused the observed chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-b13ef5ae4ba8 on the same complete frozen Search panel, with n-e4b751133c75 as matched published comparison. Observed high or near-high structures include N-F, O-F, O-O, O-S, N-O and hydrazine/thiocarbonyl motifs, plus crowded N,O-acetal-like centres. Ordinary carboxamides, ethers, tertiary amines and fused carbonyl systems are also present; one higher-scoring Child dione avoids the O-halogen linkage present in its Parent leader. The evidence supports uneven access to conservative alternatives, not impossibility of ordinary chemistry or a measured benefit from removing all unusual bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically conventional alternatives are not consistently available around high-scoring structures containing reactive heteroatom linkages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make conservative heteroatom, linker and bond replacements reachable around promising accepted graphs while preserving their local topology. Allow those alternatives to compete through the same session feedback. Do not insert objective-specific pharmacophores, infer physical utility from a score, or assume blanket liability filtering improves optimization.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-b13ef5ae4ba8, complete frozen Search panel and published comparison n-e4b751133c75. All 4350 Child proposal strings lack tetrahedral stereochemical tokens, consistent with the frozen digest, while RDKit detects potential stereocentres in 2566 rows. The Parent also has no such tokens and has 2466 rows with potential centres. The actual molecules include substituted small-ring tertiary amines, N,O-substituted methines and crowded amino/oxygen cages. This is a persistent representation gap; the trajectories supply no stereoisomer preference or causal score effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not distinguish stereochemical alternatives introduced by its substituted saturated and bridged ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where compatible with the existing identity and evaluation contract, preserve and distinguish chemically meaningful stereochemical states created by graph edits. Use current-session observations to learn whether they matter; do not prescribe a configuration or claim a score improvement without a registered measurement.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
